text: Install, check or remove the Aidus Code Scripts-menu folder in a FontLab user folder. Ported from aidus-code's install.py (archived in original/install.py). The old installer symlinked the whole plugin into FontLab's Scripts folder, replaced whatever was there, and ran uv sync for the brain. Here the host package is installed with uv pip (README), and this module only manages <user folder>/Scripts/Aidus Code : the same three thin menu scripts as the repository's Aidus Code/ folder plus a manifest ( .fontlab-aidus-code-install , format 1) holding the sha256 of every file it wrote. Ownership is per file: unknown entries are kept, a modified, foreign or symlinked entry stops an install before anything changes, and uninstall removes only unmodified owned files and the folder only when it is then empty. A folder without a valid manifest, including the workspace orchestrator's symlink, is never touched. Run on the host, not inside FontLab: fontlab-aidus-install {install,check,uninstall} .

text: The current Cocoa graphics state over a QPainter (R032). Cocoa draws through an implicit current context with a transform (CTM), a fill and stroke colour, and a save/restore stack. Here that state lives in Python: affine transforms are 6-tuples (m11, m12, m21, m22, tx, ty) composed with plain arithmetic, and a QTransform is built only when a shape is painted (no arithmetic on PythonQt wrappers; unary minus on them crashes FontLab). The base transform maps the drawing space (glyph units, or a view's y-up coordinates) to widget pixels. A context exists only inside a scope ( paint_scope for editor painters, view_scope for NSView.drawRect_ ). State operations outside one raise RuntimeError ; path painting with no destination is a no-op, as in Cocoa. A retained painter cannot paint after its callback.

text: Glyph-editor painters on FontLab's native canvas hooks (resolves R054). Builds with flCanvas.appendPythonPainter(callback, order) call Python inside the canvas paint: UnderOwner before the glyphs are drawn, OverOwner after them. callback(painter, canvas) gets a painter that FontLab has saved and reset to viewport pixels; it is valid only during the call, so this module never creates or ends one. NativeEditorPainters keeps App's registry, window poll, layer resolver and per-glyph PaintContext maths, and replaces App's transparent overlay widget with two native painters per canvas. Both phases work, so a Reporter background is really drawn under the outlines. When a canvas dies, FontLab drops its native painters itself; the destroyed slot only forgets the Python entry. editor_painters(qt, fontlab, ...) picks this class when the build has the hook, else Glyport's overlay EditorPainters (background as overlay, R054).
